text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government will not tolerate a group of irresponsible individuals handling Cyprus's foreign or internal policy. Police are seeking those who incited riots on Monday.
- Three meetings are scheduled between Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash and Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides.
- Motorcylists plan a huge protest in August to mark the murders of two Greek Cypriots last year in a similar rally.
- Suspects in riots in Nicosia on Monday night appear in court.
- The Bank of Cyprus and the Cyprus Popular Bank calculations of their stake in the Universal Life insurance company causes some confusion among investors.
- Limassol-based Options Eurocongress plans a 1.9 million pound ($3.75 million) IPO next month.
- Rapprochement concerns us all. Youths who went on the rampage on Monday night must galvanise the state into action to stop this fascist attitude.
- The government does not attach any political significance to the disturbances in Nicosia on Monday night.
- Suspects who have had a history of run-ins with police were at the demonstrations. Stones started piling up on the streets (later used in the riots) from early in the day.
- Eighteen people were remanded for disturbances in Nicosia on Monday night.
- Guards at the Nicosia central prison (close to the U.N.-controlled buffer zone) chased away three Turkish commandos who were spotted approaching the compound on Monday night.
